title: fix(gsd): scope slug-consistency warnings to rows whose arrow target is absent
body:
fix(gsd): scope slug-consistency warnings to rows whose arrow target is absent

The v1.00.30 W0 /go run emitted a false advisory:

  WARNING (slug mismatch, BUG-0041): W0 — PLAN.md targets
  waves/W0-ci-exit-truth-and-recovery-contract.md but a wave doc exists on
  disk as .planning/waves/W0-delivery-integrity-failure-freeze.md. Align the
  arrow target with the doc filename.

That remedy is wrong here and would have caused real damage.

check-slug-consistency scanned every file in .planning/waves/ matching
`^W<idx>-` and flagged any whose slug differed from the PLAN.md row. But
.planning/waves/ is shared by every campaign, and v1.00.30 and v1.00.31 both
ship W0, W1, W2, W5, W6 and W7. The second file is v1.00.31's W0, belonging to
a campaign that is complete and closed. The check has no campaign scoping, so
it reported another campaign's document as drift in the v1.00.30 plan.

Following its instruction would have re-pointed a correct arrow at a foreign
document, after which load-plan-from-index loads the WRONG content for that
wave — silently substituting one wave's doc for another's.

The fix is a one-condition scope: report a mismatch only when the row's arrow
target does NOT exist. That is the only case where there is genuinely nothing
to align but a differently-named candidate, and it is exactly the case the
pre-existing test pins. When the arrow target exists the plan already resolves
that wave unambiguously, so a co-located document from another campaign is not
drift. A missing arrow target is unaffected — it remains BUG-0023
strict-validation territory, which raises rather than warns.

Red first. New test `a co-located doc from ANOTHER campaign is not a slug
mismatch` in tests/test-wave-doc-lint.rkt fails on the unfixed code with 2
spurious mismatches, and passes after. The pre-existing `slug mismatch is
reported through the consistency surface` still passes, so the real case is
not weakened; a separate negative control confirms a genuine misnaming (arrow
target absent, only a differently-named doc present) is still reported.

Verified on the real tree: the amended v1.00.30 plan now yields 0 mismatches
and 0 warning lines, down from 1 false positive. Against the live
.planning/waves/ this also silences the equivalent W1/W2/W5/W6/W7 advisories
that share the same cause.

Two lint failures surfaced during the change and were fixed at source rather
than waived: the new test's comment contained a hard-coded version literal,
which the BUG-0009 version-expectation lint rejects in tests/ (reworded), and
metrics drifted by the lines added (regenerated canonically with
`racket scripts/metrics.rkt --tests --sync-all`; README moves only by this
change's own counts). lint-all is back to 23 passed, 2 warnings.

Verification: wave-doc lint 10/10; gsd campaign-repository 34/34; gsd
campaign-state 29/29; gsd plan-snapshot 17/17; gsd delivery-coordinator 20/20;
workflows suite 33 files / 316 tests; fast suite 1209 files / 17997 tests, 0
failed; check-deps clean; raco fmt canonical and raco make clean on both
changed files.

title: fix(release): give the release test lane full history so the recorded rehearsal head resolves
body:
fix(release): give the release test lane full history so the recorded rehearsal head resolves

The v1.00.31 release run failed in its `test` job before reaching `prepare`:
`tests/test-wave-integrity-adversarial.rkt` reported 7 passed / 1 failed, and the
failing assertion was "the rehearsal head is present in this repository"
(tests/test-wave-integrity-adversarial.rkt:216).

That test asserts the recorded `rehearsal-head` (50bdf7334) is a commit the
repository actually contains. The release `test` job checked out with the
default `fetch-depth: 1`, so a head predating the checkout tip is unresolvable
and the assertion is false in CI while true in a full clone. This was never a
property of the W6 rehearsal artifact: the recorded head is a real main
ancestor and is present in a complete clone.

This is the same defect, and the same repair, already applied in `ci.yml` for
this exact test, whose `fetch-depth: 0` comment names it. The release lane was
the sibling that was missed, which is why main CI passed and the release failed.
The `preflight` job in the same workflow already used `fetch-depth: 0` for
precisely this class of history-dependent check.

Diagnosis, not a guess. Reproduced by cloning the published `v1.00.31` tag at
depth 1 and running the test unmodified: 7 passed, 1 failed, same assertion.
`git fetch --unshallow` on that same clone makes `git cat-file -t
50bdf7334...` resolve to `commit` and the same unmodified test then passes
8/8. The fix is the checkout depth alone.

The test was deliberately NOT weakened. Making it tolerate a shallow clone
would have meant editing `tests/test-wave-integrity-adversarial.rkt`, which is
itself one of the nine digest-bound `rehearsal-inputs` in the W6 injection
matrix, so that edit would invalidate the recorded matrix and
`rehearsal-inputs-digest` and force a W6 artifact regeneration. Fixing the
checkout rather than the assertion keeps the provenance binding intact and
preserves the assertion's teeth: a genuinely fabricated head still fails.

Verification: workflows contract 7/7, purge contract 15/15, W9 workflow
verification 18/18, compiled-root workflow 113/113, CI runtime contract 38/38;
lint-all 23 passed with 2 warnings (unchanged); release notes and the
version-expectation lint over 1511 test files clean. YAML re-parsed to confirm
`fetch-depth: 0` lands on the `test` job and that no other step changed.

The annotated tag `v1.00.31` remains pointed at the release that failed; it will
be retagged at the head carrying this fix so the published release is one whose
release lane actually passed end to end.

title: feat(v1.00.31): wave 7 — blocked-wave repair, v1.00.31 bake and release (W7 of milestone #896)
body:
W7 — the final wave of the v1.00.31 GSD wave-delivery-integrity campaign (milestone #896, issue #9730, plan-id `fb67e042…`).

**Status: opened for CI verification and the final review round. NOT merge-authorized yet** — the independent review at this head has not produced an APPROVED verdict (see *Review* below). This PR will not be merged until it does.

## What this wave is

v1.00.30 never shipped a tag because its W4 wave was blocked, so this wave repairs/delivers W4 (Task 1, already merged as `cc25b3663` / bound `5f4a80fcd`, governance `governed`, status `delivered`, issue #9690 closed) and then bakes and prepares the **v1.00.31** release (Task 2).

## The substance: what the bake found

The first verification chain that *actually measured this worktree* found a defect in the test runner itself:

`resolve-base-dir` in `scripts/run-tests/classify-metadata.rkt` tried the `q`-shaped candidates before the directory it was handed. Every worktree here sits next to a `q/` clone, so a runner launched in a worktree silently collected and executed **the clone's** tests and printed a `RUN-SUMMARY` naming the clone's version. Every earlier local suite run in this campaign had been misdirected — which is why none of the following could have been found. Fixed, with 4 regression tests.

With the runner fixed, three classes of defect surfaced, all correct on `main` only while `q-version` happened to be `1.00.29`:

1. **8 test files** derived *frozen* v1.00.29-campaign artifact paths from the live version → pinned literally, reason recorded. The tier-ownership matrix is deliberately *not* pinned (it is a current-tree drift check); this milestone's copy is regenerated by the canonical generator and bound by `SHA256SUMS`.
2. **2 files unchanged from `main`** had the mirror defect — a derived value that is really a frozen *authoring identity*: the shard-plan report's `wave` field (the committed example artifact pairs it with its own `spec_reference`) and the v1.00.29 final-cohort directory (a frozen ≥20-unique-head-SHA measurement this release did not reproduce).
3. **`tests/test-worker-security.rkt` could not fail the gate at all.** Its W2 overlap checks were bare module-body cases after the file's first `run-tests`, so their failures never reached the exit code the runner reads (`failed-result?` is purely *exit code neither 0 nor 2*), and the file was reported PASSED while hiding class 1 in its own lane. Now the W2 checks are a `test-suite` run through `run-tests`, whose returned failure count drives the exit. Red-first proof: with the W2 path pointed at a nonexistent directory the file now exits 1 and reports FAILED, where the identical broken state before reported PASSED (33/33, exit 0).

Making that check able to run also exposed a fifth pre-existing failure: the strict-runner assertion was pinned to the literal pre-W4 invocation shape that this campaign's own W4 compiled-root repair had legitimately changed. It now asserts intent rather than one invocation shape.

## Coherence repairs

- The bake's own `BUG-0009` sweep had invalidated **2 of the 9 digest-bound W6 rehearsal inputs**, so the W6 matrix was regenerated by its canonical generator, its head re-stamped to the last *published* commit, `SHA256SUMS` rebound, and the report sentence claiming an unchanged inputs digest replaced with the truth.
- The W4-retained local capture's four runner-suite sections are corrected in `w4-recovery.json`, with a **true re-measurement** of the W4 head retained. W4's authoritative gates (PR #9752's 22/22, main run `36087264560`, binding, governance, status delivered) are stated as unaffected, because CI checks the branch out itself.

## Verification at the reviewed head

Full regression **1400/1401** (the one failure is `tests/test-browser-playwright-sidecar.rkt`: the `playwright` npm module does not resolve on this host — untouched by this branch, identical failure on `main` at `50bdf7334`, and the `ci` profile declares `@requires browser` so CI skips it), **fast 1209/1209**, arch 32/32, workflows 33/33, security 64/64, lint-all 23 passed, version-expectation lint 0 literals, artifact provenance green for both directories, all checksum manifests verifying from the repo root. Raw capture: `artifacts/wave-delivery-integrity/v1.00.31-w7/raw/verify-chain.txt`.

Release preflight: **6 of 7** gates pass. The 7th (`lint-release-readiness --strict`) is recorded as **deferred by design, not passed** — it is branch-gated and its `.gate-evidence` records must name the release commit and version, so it runs on clean `main` after the merge and before the tag.

## Review

Two independent read-only review rounds completed; **both returned CHANGES-REQUESTED**. All eight findings were reproduced against the tree before any fix was written, and each is fixed with its own evidence. A third round — to confirm those eight fixes and run a fresh adversarial pass at this head — **did not complete**: the reviewer tooling hit provider usage and credit limits. That is recorded in the review record as an outstanding gate, **not** as an approval. The annotated `v1.00.31` tag is pushed only after merge, a green `main`, the readiness gate, and the full CI-strict `tag-publish` preflight on clean `main`.

title: fix(delivery-controller): disable git auto-gc in the disposable test worlds
body:
## What

The push-only `test-cross-version` job (Racket 8.11) failed on `main` with
`tests/test-gsd-delivery-controller.rkt` reporting `0 passed, 1 failed` after 2m46s.

The captured per-file output showed **all 129 Python cases ran** and the single
`ERROR` was raised from the `TemporaryDirectory` finalizer:

```
oserror: [errno 39] directory not empty: 'objects'
```

## Why

`git gc --auto` can run **detached** after a commit or push, so it can still be
repacking `.git/objects` while `unittest`'s `TemporaryDirectory` cleanup walks
the fixture tree. `unittest` reports that finalizer error as a case `ERROR`
even though every assertion passed — a pure teardown race, not a behavioural
regression.

## Fix

The fixtures are disposable, so auto-gc buys nothing. `gc.auto=0` is now set in
`init_repo()` and on the bare origin, removing the race at its source rather
than masking it with `ignore_cleanup_errors=True` (which would also hide real
cleanup problems).

## Verification

- 129/129 cases pass on three consecutive local runs (~124s each)
- the Racket wrapper reports no rackunit failure
- full CI lint (18 checks) and pre-commit hooks pass

## Context

Found while completing the v1.00.30 W4 re-delivery (issue #9690): the W4
binding publication is already merged; this is a post-merge main fix following
the v1.00.31 W5 precedent, and main must be green before the W4 governance
gate can run.

body:
Closes the BUG-0072 registry entry (TUI frame corruption). Report: `.planning/bugs/BUG-0072-tui-frame-corruption-hook-error-stderr-leak/BUG_REPORT.md`.

### Root cause (two layers)
1. **Latent since #8858**: scheduler dispatches `tool-call-pre` with a `tool-pre-hook-payload` struct; `gsd-tool-guard` does `(hash-ref payload 'tool-name #f)` → contract violation on **every** scheduler tool call (hook-pass fallback let tools run; the guard was a silent no-op for 7 weeks).
2. **BUG-0068 Wave B trigger**: hook errors escalated `log-debug` → `log-error`; the default logger's stderr pump (which holds fd 2 from process start and ignores `current-error-port` parameterization) painted the exception + backtrace into the TUI frame mid-redraw → stale `[SYS]` fragments, character-interleaved rows, exception text in the prompt area.

### Fix
- **Seam (Layer 1)**: `tools/scheduler-execution.rkt` now dispatches a hash `(hasheq 'tool-name … 'tool-arguments … 'tool-call-id …)`; struct remains internal plumbing.
- **TUI stderr guard (Layer 2)**: new `tui/stderr-guard.rkt` — swaps `current-logger` to an unparented `'q-tui` logger at TUI init (default pump never sees runtime error records), surfaces each error-level record to the status line + a spill file, restores the original logger on both teardown paths. Wired in `tui/tui-init.rkt`.
- Guard regains function: executing-mode planning-artifact writes are blocked again (new test proves `'block` through the real key names).

## BUG-0069: campaign auto-retry was invisible — and the error hint lied about it

**Reported live** (2026-09-10, v1.00.29 campaign, executor session `V8CFZB5N` → `VXMB369Z`): after provider retries exhausted (`[retry: attempt 5/5]` → `[ERR] Network error contacting api.z.ai …`), the transcript's last line read **"[SYS] Error persisted after 5 retries. Type /retry to resubmit."** — while the campaign's infra-retry lane had actually resubmitted the wave automatically. The session resumed; the user had no way to know, and the advice on screen was wrong.

### Root cause (two defects, one fix)
1. `gsd.campaign.infra-retry` was emitted by the coordinator (fast lane BUG-0024-W3, slow lane BUG-0067) but had **no TUI reducer** — every automatic re-attempt was invisible.
2. `format-error-hint` is context-blind: during a campaign, a failed turn *will* be re-attempted automatically, so "Type /retry to resubmit" is false advice.

- `tui/state-events/core-handlers.rkt`: new `gsd.campaign.infra-retry` reducer → `[SYS] [wave N] infra failure — fast-lane auto-retry in 30s / slow-lane retry in 480s (6720s patience left); attempt not consumed, resuming automatically`
- `tui/state-events/helpers.rkt`: `format-error-hint` gains `#:campaign-active?` — during a campaign the hint states the automatic re-attempt ("no /retry needed"); **non-campaign hints stay byte-for-byte identical**
- `runtime/gsd-query.rkt`: `current-gsd-campaign-active-query` seam (A1-03 pattern), wired in `tui-init.rkt` from `current-gsd-campaign-owner`'s dynamic extent

title: BUG-0067: patient slow-lane infra auto-resume + settings wiring + IPC render fix
body:
## BUG-0067 (#9652): campaign infra-retry exhausts into a manual /retry on sustained provider outages — patient auto-resume with increasing delay

**Evidence (v1.00.29 launch day, campaign `6ae3ac51`):** three api.z.ai bursts in one afternoon; two exhausted the fast budget (3 × 30/60/120s ≈ 3.5 min patience) and stopped the campaign — each stop costing a manual `/retry`. Provider probes between bursts: 10/10 clean (bursty outage — exactly the class that outlasts the fast budget). Full analysis: `.planning/bugs/BUG-0067-infra-retry-budget-exhaustion-requires-manual-resume/BUG_REPORT.md`.

### Fix

**Slow lane (patient auto-resume):** when the fast budget exhausts on an infra-class failure, the coordinator keeps re-attempting the same wave with backoff that keeps **doubling** past the fast lane's 120s cap (240/480/900/900…, capped at `gsd.campaign-infra-max-delay`), until the total patience horizon (`gsd.campaign-infra-patience`, default 7200s) is consumed. Attempt is **never consumed** in either lane. Patience `0` restores the legacy fail-closed stop **byte-for-byte**. Waits are chunked (15s default) with a durable-cancellation check per chunk — a `/stop` persisted mid-backoff ends the wait within one chunk and surfaces `campaign cancelled during infra-retry backoff`.

**Settings wiring (BUG-0044 class):** `gsd.campaign-infra-retries` was documented in policy.rkt since v1.00.22 but never read by any accessor. Now wired through `settings-query.rkt` + the `settings.rkt` facade, consumed at the go-orchestrator composition root via `resolve-effective-infra-retry-policy` (keyword override > settings key > canonical default; invalid values warn-and-default — a typo'd settings file can never crash a campaign mid-wave). New keys: `gsd.campaign-infra-patience`, `gsd-campaign-infra-max-delay`.

**IPC render gap:** worker-emitted `gsd.wave.outcome-error` events cross the JSON IPC boundary with **string** keys; the TUI's keyword-only `hash-ref` rendered every such stop as `wave outcome: unknown` (the confusing line in the incident transcripts). An all-string-keyed payload is now normalized to symbol keys, so infra stops render `[infra-failed]` + the resume instruction.

### Files

- `extensions/gsd/policy.rkt` — 4 new parameters (patience, max-delay, slow-delay shape, wait-chunk)
- `extensions/gsd/infra-retry-policy.rkt` — slow-lane seams: backoff shape, patience ledger, stop messages (legacy prefix preserved), resolver, slow-state, phase-keyed telemetry (`fast`/`slow`)

title: fix(release): purge restored workspace bytecode in the release test job (BUG-0065 root cause)
body:
## fix(release): purge restored workspace bytecode in the release test job (BUG-0065 root cause)

**Root cause of all three identical release-lane failures** (cohort-report `[ASSERTION_FAILURE]` 122 passed / 5 failed, every final-claim verdict collapsed to `unverified`):

The release `test` job runs in the **prepared-env restore lane**, which skips setup-racket's `Clean stale q workspace bytecode` step (it is gated on `prepared-env.outcome != 'success'`). The restored snapshot's `.zo` files carry **mtimes newer than the fresh checkout**, so Racket's mtime invalidation trusts them and executes the **producer's bytecode instead of the checked-out sources**.

**Proof (from the run-34237587725 artifact):** the executed suite name is `final-claim verdict cohort (c3, v1.00.27 w5)` — **lowercase** — a W5-development-era source string that does not exist anywhere in the tagged tree (`tests/test-ci-cohort-report.rkt:1488` reads uppercase `(C3, v~a W5)`). CI ran old bytecode, whose rows/guard semantics predate the final W5 iteration, against the current module expectations → 5 unverified verdicts, deterministically (3/3 runs).

Local reproduction matched the mechanism exactly: editing the test file (content change → test `.zo` recompiled) over a stale module `cohort-report_rkt.zo` (mtime trusted) reproduced the exact 5 failures; purging both caches fixed it (25/25). 500/500 standalone runs passed with fully fresh caches.

### Changes

- **release.yml** `test` job: new `Purge restored workspace bytecode` step (same find as setup-racket's purge, preserving the frozen `tests/metadata-discovery/fixture`) before the fast suite — **the lane tests exactly what it checked out**.
- **tests/test-ci-cohort-report.rkt**: permanent BUG-0065 diagnostic dump — the fully-guarded gate state (per-row verdict/satisfied/reasons + guard-evidence keys) lands in per-file output on every run, so any recurrence is diagnosable from the artifact.
- **tests/test-release-workflow-contract.rkt**: contract pins the purge step and the diagnostics so neither can regress.

### Supersedes

The campaign's "stale compiled bytecode — invalidated via instrumented no-op recompile" checkpoint (`40f3fc16`) saw the same class and treated it as local hygiene; the lane-level root cause is fixed here.

Refs #9622. Milestone #892.

## BUG-0062 (#9596): GSD events never reached TUI reducers

`apply-event-to-state` dispatched reducers via a raw hash lookup on `(event-ev evt)`, but the registry is keyed by **strings** while every live GSD emitter passes **symbols** (`emit-gsd-event! title: fix: surface coordinator-owned verification progress in the TUI (#9584)
body:
## BUG-0058 — coordinator-owned GSD verification is invisible in the TUI

Closes #9584.

### Problem
After a wave executor returns its final response, `/go` runs the declared Verify command in the coordinator-owned verification lane, but the TUI kept displaying the executor summary. A healthy multi-minute gate looked like a hang, encouraging operators to interrupt valid verification (observed live during v1.00.24 W4: 380 s gate, durable campaign advanced, TUI unchanged).

### Fix (visibility-only; verifier ownership/timeout/cancellation semantics unchanged)
- **Coordinator emissions** (`delivery-verifier.rkt`, `registry-run-verify`):
  - `gsd.verification.started` — wave, command, bounded timeout, durable log path, attach flag, start time.
  - `gsd.verification.completed` — terminal state, exit code, reducer-compatible `verdict`/`reason`, real elapsed seconds, log path.
  - Emission is best-effort; a bus failure can never affect verification. No log contents are emitted — only paths, timings, and exit codes.
- **TUI state** (`state-types.rkt`): new `verification-progress` field on `streaming-state` (hash or `#f`) with `ui-state-verification-progress` / `set-verification-progress`.
- **Reducers** (`core-handlers.rkt`): started renders `W<N> verifying — budget <t>s · log <path>` and stores the start time; completed clears progress and enriches rejection entries with elapsed + log path. Legacy `artifact-count` payloads render byte-identically to before.
- **Status bar** (`render/status-line.rkt`): live `Xm Ys elapsed` suffix while the gate is active — the report's "4m12s elapsed" acceptance criterion.
- **Inventory**: `delivery-verifier` deps now include `events` (responsibility inventory).

### Tests
- Coordinator regression: failing declared verify emits started + completed with wave, timeout, log path, verdict `reject`, exit code, real elapsed, state-naming reason (`test-gsd-delivery-verifier.rkt`, 24/24).
- TUI regressions (`test-tui-verification-display.rkt`, 20/20): wave-scoped status + stored progress; approve clears status/progress; reject entry carries elapsed (`4m 12s`) + log; status bar renders live elapsed (`1m Ns`) and nothing when inactive; legacy payload compatibility retained.

title: fix: bounded same-wave verification repair with exact diagnostics (#9583)
body:
## BUG-0060 — verification failure gets no repair retry

Closes #9583.

### Problem
When the coordinator's declared Verify chain rejected a delivered wave, `run-campaign-wave` persisted `failed` and stopped the campaign with no same-wave repair attempt. The verifier's command/exit/log diagnostics never reached a successor executor, and the delivered worktree/branch evidence was at risk on the failure path.

### Fix (bounded, at-least-once, fail-closed)
- **Classification**: only an owned declared-Verify subprocess failure (evidence pair `("verify" #f "cmd=... exit=... log=...")`) is repairable. Boolean/blank verdicts and repository/branch/evidence failures stay terminal.
- **Budget**: new `current-gsd-wave-verification-repair-retries` (default `1`), independent from no-change and infra retry budgets. Each repair consumes a fresh fenced attempt (`begin-attempt!`), preserving D5 at-least-once semantics.
- **Work preserved**: the repair attempt continues on the SAME branch/worktree via `call-with-retained-wave-worktree!` (new in wave-executor.rkt); every attempt still records a truthful artifact-ledger entry. A no-progress guard stops repair when the branch head is unchanged.
- **Exact diagnostics**: the delivery verifier's failing evidence now embeds a bounded `failed-output-summary` (last 4 KiB of combined output), and `verification-repair-context-block` carries the verifier message verbatim into the successor prompt with an explicit "rerun the COMPLETE declared Verify chain" completion rule.
- **Fail-closed exhaustion**: budget exhaustion or no branch progress emits `gsd.verification.repair-exhausted` (new event; `repair-started` on retry) and produces a truthful terminal `wave-failed` with the verifier reason.
- **Size discipline (BUG-0042)**: `wave-outcome-reporting.rkt` extracted from `go-orchestrator.rkt`; file 1499 → 1497 lines, 24 → 22 defines; `go-orchestrator-baseline.rktd` re-recorded in the same commit per the fixture's maintenance contract.

- parameter-inventory: `current-gsd-wave-verification-repair-retries` (CONFIGURATION), total 228 → 229

title: chore(deps): bump actions/download-artifact from 7 to 8
body:
Bumps [actions/download-artifact](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact) from 7 to 8.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/download-artifact's releases.

v8.0.0

v8 - What's new

[!IMPORTANT] actions/download-artifact@v8 has been migrated to an ESM module. This should be transparent to the caller but forks might need to make significant changes.

[!IMPORTANT] Hash mismatches will now error by default. Users can override this behavior with a setting change (see below).

Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in actions/upload-artifact, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the Content-Type header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new skip-decompress parameter to true.

Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the digest-mismatch parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to error which will fail the workflow run.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

What's Changed

  • Don't attempt to un-zip non-zipped downloads by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#460
  • Add a setting to specify what to do on hash mismatch and default it to error by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#461
